healthcareSystem: Limited public healthcare system. Vila Central Hospital in Port Vila is the main facility. Outer islands have only basic health centers or aid posts. Private clinics in Port Vila offer better care for routine issues.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is basic. Vila Central Hospital handles emergencies but has limited equipment. English and French are official languages — medical staff generally speak both plus Bislama. Serious conditions require evacuation to Australia or New Zealand.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in Port Vila open 8am-5pm weekdays, 8am-12pm Saturday. No pharmacies on outer islands.
pharmacyTips: Very limited pharmacy options. Only Port Vila and Luganville have pharmacies. Stock is inconsistent. Bring all needed medications from home. English and Bislama spoken.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is minimal. Limited medication availability makes it essential to bring all needed medications. English documentation accepted.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications. Keep medications in original packaging. English documentation is accepted. Bring generous extra supplies for outer island travel.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation is essential. Evacuation to Australia or New Zealand costs $50,000-150,000. Ensure coverage includes diving, snorkeling, and adventure activities.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Malaria risk exists on some islands — consult a travel doctor. Dengue fever is present.

waterNotes: Tap water is not reliably safe. Use bottled water or boiled/treated water, especially outside Port Vila. Resorts generally provide safe drinking water. Rainwater tanks on outer islands may be contaminated.
foodSafetyTips: Food at established restaurants is generally safe. Be cautious with reef fish due to ciguatera poisoning risk — ask locals about safe species. Eat cooked food served hot. Lap-lap (national dish) and island cuisine from reputable restaurants is safe.
medicalTourismNote: Vanuatu is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring specialist care are evacuated to Australia (Brisbane, Sydney) or New Zealand (Auckland).
metaDescription: Health guide for Vanuatu: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, water safety tips, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Vila Central Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital in Vanuatu. Emergency department. Basic but handles most routine cases. English and French spoken.

hospitals.name: ProMedical
hospitals.notes: Private medical clinic. Better standard of care. Popular with tourists and expats.

hospitals.name: Northern District Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main hospital for Santo Island. Basic emergency care. Useful for tourists visiting WWII sites and blue holes.

hospitals.name: Medical Services Pacific (MSP)
hospitals.notes: Private medical and dental clinic. Good reputation for traveler care.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. A few dental clinics in Port Vila only.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is basic. MSP clinic in Port Vila offers dental services. Equipment may be limited.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Medical Services Pacific (MSP) in Port Vila has a dental clinic. For serious dental issues, evacuation to Australia may be needed.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. A few counselors available through NGOs in Port Vila.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited. Bring all psychiatric medications from home.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is very limited. Most buildings, paths, and beaches lack wheelchair access. Terrain is rough and hilly.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Vila Central Hospital has basic ground-floor access. Most clinics lack proper accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads are rough. Private transfers can be arranged.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Vanuatu is challenging for travelers with mobility impairments. Beach resorts may have some flat access. Confirm accessibility with specific accommodations in advance. Outer islands are particularly difficult.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited testing available at Vila Central Hospital.
covidStatus.notes: Dengue, ciguatera fish poisoning, cyclone season (November-April), and sun exposure are more relevant health concerns.

insuranceClaimProcess: Hospitals and clinics require upfront cash payment (Vatu or AUD/USD accepted at some facilities). Keep all receipts. English documentation provided.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Local currency is Vanuatu Vatu (VUV). Costs vary significantly between public and private facilities.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is essential for Vanuatu travel. Local healthcare is very basic. Brisbane is the nearest major medical hub (approximately 3-hour flight).
